blocks.text: Setting up Notion for support workflows

The first step is installing the Notion desktop app on your Mac. Ensure you are running macOS 13 or later. Once installed, create a dedicated workspace for your support team. Use a database to track common customer requests. This allows you to filter by status, priority, or agent assigned.

Support agents need to move fast. Use slash commands to format your notes instantly. Type / followed by a command to add a callout, table, or checkbox. This keeps your documentation clean without needing to click through menus.

A shared knowledge base prevents repetitive work. Document common solutions in a central page. Link these pages directly in your help desk tools. This ensures every agent provides the same accurate information to customers.

When you handle high volumes, use database templates. Create a template for bug reports or feature requests. This forces consistent data entry across your team. You can then use filters to see only the items that need immediate attention.

blocks.text: Mastering shortcuts saves hours every week. Use ⌘ + P to open the search bar instantly. Press Shift + ? to see all available shortcuts in the app. These small habits add up during a busy shift.

faq.question: Is Notion free for small support teams?
faq.answer: Notion offers a free plan for individuals. For teams, you may need a paid plan depending on your storage and member requirements.

faq.question: Can I use Notion offline on my Mac?
faq.answer: The Notion desktop app requires an internet connection to sync your data. It does not support a true offline mode for editing.

faq.question: How do I move my existing support docs to Notion?
faq.answer: You can import CSV files or use the copy and paste function for most text-based documents. Notion also supports Markdown imports.
